# Motion grammar (distilled from 28 professional launch films)

These principles came from studying 28 professionally produced SaaS launch films (48 minutes, 81,647 frames numerically analysed, plus sampled visual study of every film and dense frame-by-frame study of key transitions). Per-film notes are in `launch-film-notes.md`.

## The six rules

1. **The foreground becomes the transition.** A headline, logo or shape scales through the camera, with directional blur and stretched edges, while the next scene is already in place underneath. There's no empty gap between scenes. (Contra "Creative Arena", Wonder, Bolt.)
2. **One persistent actor.** A selected photo, cursor, card, rail or measured shape keeps its identity across shots. Unrelated reveals in sequence feel like a slideshow however well each one is animated. (Wonder's cursor, Replit's rails, Poke's request bubble.)
3. **Density comes from hierarchy.** One primary camera/object move, supporting staggers on cards and labels, and fine tertiary detail (edge sweeps, status ticks), all overlapping. Don't start and stop the whole frame on every beat. (Taste's artifact ring, Wonder's canvas.)
4. **Change speed; don't drift at a constant rate.** Readable target → fast exit → slowing arrival. Motion eases into a landing so the viewer can read, then leaves quickly.
5. **Smooth doesn't mean dissolves only.** Hard cuts work when subject, scale, direction and material language match and motion continues after the cut. (Work Louder cuts from parallax keyboards straight into an exploded view.)
6. **Show the business purpose as cause → effect.** Scans produce findings, prompts produce artifacts, buttons produce states. Every animated action should visibly produce a result. (Contra's scanning counter → results; Bolt's merge button → "ready".)

## Composition rules that follow

- The lead subject fills 60–85% of the usable frame in feature beats. Empty space reads as cheap to buyers.
- Vary composition types: physical macro, wide dimensional, overhead/plan, UI close-up, typographic impact. Don't repeat "heading above three cards".
- Keep 1–2 reading targets at a time. Dense doesn't mean everything competes.
- Type is part of the choreography: oversized words enter on opposing axes, mask or reveal the next scene, and never sit still over busy footage without a backing.
- Hand objects across scenes at exact pixel coordinates. Pre-position the destination so the carried object lands on it.
- Keep one wipe direction and one title position through a sequence of similar shots. The outgoing title leaves before the wipe; the incoming title enters after it.

## Mechanism catalog (reusable moves)

| Mechanism | What it does | Seen in |
|---|---|---|
| Foreground fly-through | Claim/logo scales past the camera, revealing a pre-positioned next scene | Contra 24, Wonder 19, Bolt 25 |
| Logo-as-portal | The brand shape grows until its hole becomes the next frame | Bolt 25 |
| Selection → expansion | A selected frame expands into the detailed workspace for the next beat | Wonder 18/19, AsideHQ 05 |
| Materializing result | A shell appears first, then its internal regions fill in order | Replit Slides 11 |
| Persistent rails | Lines/paths survive a text swap and connect two states | Replit 13 |
| Continuous canvas | The camera moves over one spatial layout; the selected item stays sharp while neighbours blur | Replit Canvas 12 |
| Artifact ring | Many small artifacts orbit a stable centre sentence | Taste 10 |
| Card stack / fan | Screens arrive and occlude; one card becomes a collection, or a collection resolves to one | Bevel 16, Tembo 26 |
| Perspective fold | A panel folds to a luminous strip; the next panel rises out of it | AgentArcade 21 |
| Exploded layers | A product separates into its physical layers, then recombines | Work Louder 22 |
| Registered decomposition | The source artifact stays recognisable while regions lift into categories | Extend 28 |
| Wall → one actor | Information overload collapses to a single clear subject | Contra 23 |
| Carousel emphasis | A rotating list with one bright active item and receding neighbours | MadeThis 20 |
| Colour-field takeover | A soft gradient cloud fills the frame for a brand handoff (use once, not as the main vocabulary) | Conduit 27 |
| Tile wipe | A grid of tiles as a chapter break (fragmented, use sparingly) | Pilot Protocol 15 |
| Request → picker → confirmation | A message bubble anchors while a sheet rises, a choice is made, and the state confirms | Poke 17 |

## Pacing numbers that worked (30s business film)

- About 12–15 compositions; beats of 1.4–3.5s; no motionless stretch over ~0.6s.
- Hook: frame 0 must be a finished composition, not a half-entered word.
- Reading holds only on the few frames that carry the business message (report, CTA); even there, a slow 3–5% push keeps it alive.
- End card: about 1.5–2s readable, with gentle drift.
